title: Osaka for Two: Street food, neon lights & late-winter charm
description: Three days exploring Osaka’s legendary food scene, retro neighborhoods, and cultural highlights — with early plum blossoms hinting at spring. Perfect for a couple craving takoyaki by the canal and quiet moments in hidden alleys.

days.title: Namba, Dotonbori & the Neon Heart of Osaka
days.description: Dive straight into Osaka’s most electric neighborhood. Today is all about the iconic canal, legendary street food, and atmospheric alleys.

activities.name: Check Into Hotel Nikko Osaka
activities.description: Steps from Shinsaibashi and Dotonbori. Request a higher floor for city views. Stroll along the canal past the giant Glico Running Man sign, the moving crab at Kani Doraku, and dozens of neon facades. Late February crowds are thinner than peak season — perfect for photos.

activities.name: Hozenji Yokocho Alley
activities.description: Atmospheric stone-paved lane just off Dotonbori. Visit moss-covered Hozenji Temple and splash water on the Fudo Myo-o statue for good luck as a couple. 20-minute boat ride along the canal. Neon signs reflected on the water at night — genuinely romantic. ¥900 per person.

days.title: Osaka Castle, Kuromon Market & Shinsekai
days.description: From a morning feast at Osaka’s 120-year-old market to plum blossoms at the castle and retro vibes in Shinsekai — today covers the city’s soul.

activities.name: Osaka Castle & Plum Grove
activities.description: The castle is stunning in winter light. By late February the plum grove in Nishinomaru Garden should show early blossoms — pink and white against the castle walls. Entry ¥200.

activities.name: Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku Tower
activities.description: Retro neighborhood frozen in 1960s Osaka. Puffer fish lanterns, vintage arcades, and the iconic tower. Rub Billiken’s feet for good luck.

activities.name: Spa World
activities.description: Massive onsen complex with baths themed after countries worldwide. Perfect for warming up on a cold February evening. Tattoo-friendly hours available.

days.title: Umeda Sky, Nakazakicho & Farewell Bites
days.description: Final morning heads north to Osaka’s modern skyline, a hidden café village, and Japan’s longest shopping arcade before one last bowl of ramen.

activities.name: Nakazakicho Neighborhood Walk
activities.description: Hidden gem north of Umeda — converted machiya townhouses turned into tiny cafes, galleries, and bookshops. Feels like a secret village. Wander without a map.

activities.name: Umeda Sky Building Floating Garden
activities.description: Twin towers connected 170 meters up with panoramic Kansai views. On a clear day, see to Awaji Island. The luminous rooftop walkway is gorgeous for couples. Japan’s longest covered arcade — 2.6 km. Grab last-minute omiyage: Osaka Kit Kats, tenugui towels, local snacks.

editorialSummary: Three days exploring Osaka’s legendary food scene, retro neighborhoods, and cultural highlights — with early plum blossoms hinting at spring. Perfect for a couple craving takoyaki by the canal and quiet moments in hidden alleys.
